To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the flavescence dor ee (FD) phytoplasma is present in Croatian vineyards and that it belongs to the mapFD1, FD2 and FD3 clusters, and that it is also present in Ailanthus trees and the leafhopper Ph. cyclops.

flavescence dor e phytoplasma was found in Croatia for first time, that three distinct flavescenc dor e phytoplassma genetic clusters were found, that flavescence dore phytoplasma has been found in invasive Ailanthus alitissima tree and in leafhopper Phlogettix cyclops, that high genetic variability was found among isolates, that different routes of introduction and propagation were found, and that complex ecological cycle was found.

flavescence dor ee (FD) phytoplasmas have been identified in Croatia for the very first time in alders and in the invasive tree species, Ailanthus, and in the leafhopper Phlogetettix cyclops, and that three different FDp genetic clusters were identified in Croatian vineyards.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first detection of FDp and its genetic diversity in Croatia.
the first report of FDp in Croatia and its first molecular characterization.
the identification and characterization of FDp strains in the vineyards of Croatia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Croatia represents a new FDp endemic area, with an important role of A. altissima as an alternative host and reservoir for FDp.
FDp is present throughout Croatia and is transmitted mainly by S. titanus, which was found to be a vector of all three FDp genetic clusters.
FDp was introduced in Croatia from Italy, and that it is now spreading in the country.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MLST method proved to be useful in characterizing and tracing the spread of FDp in Croatia.
the FDp genetic clusters are present in Croatia, but the disease is still under control.

Croatia is not only a country where FDp has been detected for the first time, but also a country with the highest genetic variability of FDp in Europe, which is of high concern for the grapevine cultivation in the region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MLST approach is a powerful tool for phytoplasma strain identification and for tracing transmission pathways.
the MLST analysis is an efficient tool for FDp strain characterization and identification.

the presence of three genetic clusters in Croatia suggests the existence of multiple pathways of FDp introduction, which may be associated with the different geographical origin of FDp strains and their introduction by different vectors.
